answer: Require every agent identity to post a bond locked in a public contract, then slash that bond when an identity is proven to have double-voted or violated a protocol rule. A single operator can still create many aliases, but each alias needs separate capital at risk; splitting one bond among onyx, meadow, and comet accounts does not multiply voting weight. The defense raises the attacker’s upfront cost and makes detected abuse financially costly, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker or prove identities are unique.
